body.x: CES 2025, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition, concluded on January 10 (local time) in Las Vegas, USA. The event featured the largest-ever "Seoul Pavilion," which drew significant attention from global visitors.

This year's Seoul Pavilion, spanning 1,040 square meters, was set up at Eureka Park, CES’s startup exhibition zone. The pavilion showcased Seoul’s startup ecosystem and began with an opening ceremony on January 7 at 10 a.m. and continued for four days.

The pavilion was a collaborative effort among three Seoul districts (Gangnam, Gwanak, and Geumcheon), five startup support organizations (Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Campus Town Growth Center), and eight major Seoul-based universities (Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kookmin University, Sogang University, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Yonsei University, Chung-Ang University, and Seoul National University).

At the opening ceremony, representatives from 16 participating organizations and 104 companies, along with 103 supporters, declared their vision for "Team Seoul" and announced their ambitions to take on the global tech stage.

Under the slogan “Team Seoul, ON BOARD to Dive in!” Representatives from 16 organizations took the stage for a "boarding ceremony," and student supporters in the audience used “Green Aurora” glow sticks to mark the start of the Seoul Pavilion.

Representing one of Seoul’s major universities, Sogang University participated in the Seoul Pavilion with ten companies, including faculty-led startups recruited through the Industry-Academia Cooperation Foundation.

This marked the university’s third appearance at CES. Since establishing its Industry-Academia Cooperation Foundation in 2004, Sogang University has been actively supporting R&D-focused activities and fostering startups. Initially managing an external research fund of 10 billion KRW, the foundation has grown to handle over 60 billion KRW, bolstered by numerous large-scale research projects.

The foundation has also been advancing by actively establishing joint ventures with its tech holding company. This has allowed it to consolidate and expand the university’s infrastructure, creating a leading industry-academia collaboration model.

Sogang University’s foundation has been building a business-friendly industry-academia collaboration system, completing joint commercialization platforms, specializing in human resources, and nurturing seed-stage businesses in emerging industries. Using its CES 2025 participation as a springboard, it aims to accelerate the global expansion of promising startups and promote "K-technology" worldwide.

During CES 2025, Sogang University attracted multinational visitors and showcased its roadmap for corporate-driven economic growth in Seoul. AVING News interviewed Kwanwoo Shin to learn more about the university’s plans.

body.cap: Kwanwoo Shin, Head of Sogang University’s Industry-Academia Cooperation Foundation, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q. AVING News: This is Sogang University’s third participation in CES. How was this year’s experience?

A. Kwanwoo Shin: I was amazed by the diversity and innovation of startups showcasing cutting-edge technologies and solutions centered around AI. Witnessing the progress and development of Sogang University’s CES journey fills me with pride.

Compared to other universities in Seoul, Sogang University sent the largest number of undergraduates to CES 2025. These 30 students actively introduced local businesses to visitors and facilitated smooth communication between corporate representatives, global media, potential customers, and partners.
Through these efforts, we have strengthened the synergy between the university, its foundation, and the companies we support, contributing significantly to their global business endeavors.
Q. AVING News: How were the companies representing Sogang University at CES 2025 selected?

A. Kwanwoo Shin: Previously, we focused on faculty-led startups. This year, we expanded by recruiting promising startups through a public call facilitated by our foundation. We selected ten companies based on strict criteria evaluating their technological, product, and service innovation.

Two companies under Sogang University’s umbrella received Innovation Awards this year. This strategy led to accolades and significantly increased the number of visitors to our booths during the exhibition.

body.cap: Kwanwoo Shin, Head of Sogang University’s Industry-Academia Cooperation Foundation, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q. AVING News: Could you highlight companies that stood out at CES 2025?

A. Kwanwoo Shin: One standout is SCALe Virtual Inc (CEO Tesoc Hah)., which unveiled the MYVRS Virtual Pod, a mobile virtual studio. It comprises XR hardware and a proprietary app and digitizes individuals into virtual online environments. The product’s booth attracted substantial attention, reflecting the high value of its CES Innovation Award.

Another highlight is Cubic-K (CEO Kim Dongchoul), which showcased Quantix, a next-generation bioreactor measurement solution. Founded by professors from Sogang University, the company integrates advanced nanomaterials and AI capabilities for real-time molecular analysis. Cubic-K has already garnered significant interest from domestic and international industries.

body.cap: Kwanwoo Shin, Head of Sogang University’s Industry-Academia Cooperation Foundation, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q. AVING News: What are Sogang University’s plans following CES 2025?

A. Kwanwoo Shin: We plan to analyze the insights and networks gained from CES 2025 and address shortcomings. Our goal is to create an even more refined exhibition for CES 2026. This experience will also serve as a foundation for enhancing our strategy to cultivate global talent, benefit businesses, and drive advancements across Korea’s industries.
Sogang University aims to foster progress and innovation on a broad scale by seamlessly integrating business and education.

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
